quote: Every document in the package is governed by New York law and subject to New York County jurisdiction except the TSA, which selects Delaware law and Delaware courts... APA § 10.12 (Order of Precedence), which provides that the APA controls over the Ancillary Agreements "except that each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its specific subject matter." One could argue that a document's own governing-law clause is part of its "specific subject matter," meaning the TSA's Delaware choice might survive... creates the possibility of inconsistent interpretations across the deal documents... Replace TSA § 9.3 with: ... governed by ... the Laws of the State of New York ... exclusive jurisdiction of the State and federal courts located in New York County, New York
reason: The memo meets every element of the criterion. It identifies TSA § 9.3's Delaware law and Delaware forum as conflicting with the APA's New York law and New York County forum. It explains that APA § 10.12 lets the TSA control as to its own subject matter, so the Delaware clause may survive and the conflict is not cured. It notes the risk of inconsistent outcomes across the deal documents. It does not name the fee set-off example, but it captures the same concern about split forums and bodies of law. It also gives a full replacement clause conforming the TSA to New York law and New York County courts.
